anchor: Everything is for a term remarkable in navies
note: For a term: for a time. Navies make monuments of objects tied to striking incidents.
A boom is a spar. The yard-arm was cut down and used as an ordinary boom in a naval dockyard.
Christians kept splinters said to come from the cross of Jesus as holy relics. The sailors treat the spar so.
Wilful: done on purpose. The sailors know Billy could not murder.

anchor: never deformed by a sneer or subtler vile freak of the heart
note: Freak: a sudden odd whim. Billy’s face never showed meanness.
Artless: natural, simple, without art or cunning.

anchor: finally got rudely printed at Portsmouth as a ballad
note: A ballad is a popular narrative song. Cheap printed ballads sold in seaports.
Darbies: handcuffs or leg irons.

anchor: down on his marrow-bones here and pray
note: Marrow-bones: knees. To go down on one’s marrow-bones is to kneel.

anchor: It tips the guard’s cutlas and silvers this nook
note: A cutlass is a short curved sword. A nook is a small corner.

anchor: A jewel-block they’ll make of me to-morrow
note: A jewel-block is a pulley at a yard-arm end that carries studding-sails outward. He will dangle there, like a jewel.
Pendant: hanging down. He will hang from the yard-arm like a jewel.

anchor: Like the ear-drop I gave to Bristol Molly
note: An ear-drop is a hanging earring. Bristol Molly is the sweetheart he gave one to.
Alow: below. He will go aloft from the deck below.
To hoist is to haul up, to belay to make fast. Sailors turn away from the hanging work.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Belay”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

note: Halyards are ropes that hoist sails. A pipe was a boatswain’s whistle that signaled when hoisting began.

anchor: A hatchet to my hawser? all adrift to go?
note: A hawser is a thick rope. Cutting it with a hatchet sets a ship adrift.
A drum roll called the crew to receive their daily ration of grog.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Grog”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

note: The plank is the board from which a body is slid into the sea.
Taff is a sailors’ nickname for a Welshman.

anchor: his cheek it was like the budding pink
note: Pink: a flower, here the blush of a dead man’s cheek.
The dead were sewn in their hammocks for burial at sea.
A fathom is six feet of water depth.

anchor: Just ease this darbies at the wrist
note: He asks the sentry to loosen the handcuffs.

anchor: the oozy weeds about me twist
note: Oozy: slimy and muddy. Seaweed on the sea floor wraps round him.
